intro: How your team talks to each other and to the people outside: messages and channels with colleagues, calls and meetings in your own rooms, announcements for everyone, and the email addresses, numbers and chat accounts that conversations with customers come in through.
start: Connect your email address, number or chat account in Channels, so conversations with customers come in and replies go out.
Say what each chat account is for in Chat platforms: customer conversations, Capture or the assistant.
Open Messages and make a channel for a team or a topic.
Try Start now on Meet, so you know how the waiting screen and the room work before your first meeting with a customer.

articles.title: Send a message to a colleague
articles.summary: Write to one colleague, or a few at once, and attach files or name a document in the same message.

steps.rest: at the top right of Messages, and choose Message.
One colleague is a conversation between the two of you; up to eight make a group.
It opens beside the list.
Enter sends, and Shift Enter adds a line. They are told when you write.

tips: Use the paperclip to attach a file, and Link a document to name an invoice or a quotation. A colleague sees the document's details only if they may read it.
Save keeps a message under Saved. Pin keeps it at the top of the chat for everyone in it.
People cannot be added to a group later. Start a new message with everyone you want in it.

articles.title: Make a channel for a team or a topic
articles.summary: A place to talk about one thing: say who it is for and who can find it, then invite the people you want.

steps.rest: on Messages and choose Channel.

steps.lead: Give it a name and a topic,
steps.rest: and choose who it is for and who may find it: public, or private for those invited.
if you want to, now or later.
It shows in the list, and the people you invited are in it.

tips: A channel for a department or a team takes its staff in, and lets them go when they move. A channel for everyone is always public.
Others find public channels with Browse channels and press Join. Mute stops a busy channel from telling you about every message.
Every meeting gets a private channel of its own, with what was said in the room, its files and its recording.

articles.title: Call the people in a chat
articles.summary: Press Call in a channel or a direct message and everyone else in it is rung. The call is left as a card in the thread.

steps.lead: Open the channel or the direct message.
steps.rest: You need to be in it.
Everyone else in it is rung, with their voice only to start.
or join from the card the call leaves in the thread.
When the room empties, the card closes and says how long the call lasted.

tips: A ring nobody answers in thirty seconds becomes a missed call in their Inbox, with Call back.
Someone who cannot talk can decline and reply with a message instead. It goes to your direct message.

articles.title: Start a meeting now and let people in
articles.summary: Open your own room in one step, choose camera or voice, share the code and let in the people who knock.

steps.rest: on Meet. Your room opens on the waiting screen.

steps.lead: Choose Join with video or Join with voice only.
steps.rest: Voice only is lighter on a slow connection. You can turn the camera on later.

steps.lead: Share the room code, or press Copy the link.
steps.rest: Colleagues come straight in. Anyone else says their name and waits to be let in.
beside each person waiting, or Turn away.
when you are done. A meeting started now ends once the room is empty.

tips: Lock the meeting to stop anyone else joining. Those waiting are told.
A recording is filed in the organiser's own Drive, in a folder called Meeting recordings.
A meeting started now is on your calendar like any other, with its record, chat and files. Start it again opens the same room for another hour.

articles.title: Join a meeting with its code
articles.summary: Type the room code from the invitation, or scan the QR on the host's screen, and choose camera or voice.

steps.lead: Type the code into Room code
steps.rest: on the Join card, or press Scan to read the QR on the host's screen.
The waiting screen opens.

steps.lead: Choose Join with video or Join with voice only.
steps.rest: You are in, or you wait until a host lets you in.

tips: A code is your organisation's short name and eight letters and digits. It can be typed as it was heard, in capitals or not, with or without the gaps.
The invitation email and the meeting on your calendar both carry Join the meeting.

articles.title: Have the minutes of a meeting written for you
articles.summary: For a meeting in the room with you: the assistant listens, then gives you minutes and drafts to confirm.
before: Your organisation must allow meetings to be recorded. If it does not, the Take notes card says so.

steps.rest: on the Take notes card when the meeting begins.
Pause and Resume as you need. The meeting is on your calendar, without a room.
when the meeting ends.
You are told when the minutes are set out, with how many drafts there are to check.

steps.lead: Confirm, change or turn down each draft.
steps.rest: A task or a message is made only when you confirm it. Nothing is sent before.

articles.title: Tell everyone something with an announcement
articles.summary: Write it once, say how urgent it is and who it is for, and see who has read or acknowledged it.

steps.rest: on Announcements.
a title, and the words in plain language.
low, normal, high or critical. A critical one stays on top of every screen until it is acknowledged.

steps.lead: Say who it is for, and when.
steps.rest: With nothing chosen, it goes to everyone. Set Publish at to send it later, and Expires at to take it out of the feed.

steps.lead: Choose how people outside the app are reached,
steps.rest: and tick Ask everyone to acknowledge it if they must confirm they read it.
Where an approval policy asks, the button is Send for approval, and nothing goes until it is approved.

articles.after: Open the announcement to see who it reached, who read it and who acknowledged it. Remind who has not acknowledged sends them a nudge.
tips: Opening an announcement marks it read for you. A critical one asks you to press I have read and understood this.
Retract takes a published announcement back.

articles.title: Connect an email address, number or chat account
articles.summary: Add your own address or account, so conversations with customers come in through it and replies go out through it.

steps.rest: on Channels.

steps.lead: Choose what it is and its provider,
steps.rest: then give it a name and the address or number it sends from.
They are sealed when saved and never shown again.
primary, or a backup that is tried when the primary fails.
Then press Copy webhook and give the address to your provider, or Copy website snippet for website chat.

tips: A channel that keeps failing says so, with the error, on its row.
Retire stops a channel sending and taking in. Its conversations stay.
Until you connect a channel, people outside are reached by email with a link.

articles.title: Choose what a chat account is used for
articles.summary: Each chat account can carry customer conversations, take documents into Capture, and let colleagues talk to the assistant.
before: Connect the account first, in Channels.

steps.rest: Each account shows what came in and went out this week, and how many colleagues linked their chat.

steps.lead: Press What it is used for
steps.rest: on the account.
Customer conversations, Capture, or The assistant.

steps.lead: Say who files from outside are kept with,
steps.rest: and the welcome words someone new is sent, if you want any.

steps.lead: Press Save what it is used for.
steps.rest: Then Check the connection to see that it works.

tips: Colleagues link their own chat to their sign-in from Link my chat. The chat then acts as them, with their own permissions.
Nothing the assistant proposes in a chat is done until the colleague confirms it.
An account in sandbox mode talks to no real platform. Use its Sandbox console to try messages as someone writing in.

articles.title: See what is sent, and set the limits
articles.summary: Every message passes one gate. See what was sent, what waits and what failed, and set how much may go out.

steps.rest: The figures show what was sent today, what is waiting for room, what failed and what was not repeated.
to list the messages that did not go, with the reason for each.
Set how many messages each channel may send in a minute, an hour and a day, and how many one person may get.

steps.lead: Set quiet hours if you want them,
steps.rest: and read What this changes, worked out from today's traffic.
The change takes effect within half a minute.

tips: Over a limit, a message waits for the next window and goes then. It is never dropped.
Reminders, notifications and summaries wait out the quiet hours. Codes, and what a person sends by hand, are not held.
